summary: GCS-backed asset browser: renders Jinja2 HTML pages to navigate bucket directories at a given prefix, proxies raw object bytes for download, displays image assets (PNG/SVG) in a dedicated HTML viewer, renders Markdown articles fetched from GCS, and provides a bulk sync CLI to upload the local curricula/SAT/ directory to the bucket.

evidence.claim: GET /browse renders an HTMLResponse via Jinja2 listing GCS bucket objects at a given prefix
GET /object/{key} streams raw GCS object bytes as a proxy download with content-type headers
GET /image/{key} renders an HTML page displaying a GCS-stored image asset with navigation breadcrumbs
GET /view/{key} renders an HTML page displaying a Markdown article fetched from GCS
sync_sat_to_gcs.py walks curricula/SAT/ and uploads all files to GCS, supports --dry-run flag
browse endpoint calls reader.list_prefix(prefix) on a GcsReader dependency to enumerate bucket contents

invariants.statement: All five surfaces share a single GCS read/listing concern via the GcsReader dependency
The sync script uploads to the same GCS bucket that the browse/object/image/view surfaces read from
HTML rendering uses Jinja2 templates injected via FastAPI dependency

scenarios.name: browse bucket root
scenarios.given: A GCS bucket containing generated question assets
scenarios.when: GET /browse is requested with no prefix
scenarios.then: An HTML page listing the top-level bucket objects and subdirectories is returned

scenarios.name: download raw asset
scenarios.given: A known GCS object key from the browse listing
scenarios.then: The raw object bytes are streamed back with correct content-type headers

scenarios.name: view image asset
scenarios.given: A GCS key pointing to a PNG or SVG file
scenarios.then: An HTML page embedding the image with a back-navigation link is returned

scenarios.name: bulk upload curricula
scenarios.then: All files are uploaded to the GCS bucket and become visible via /browse

options: Server-side Jinja2 templates rendered by FastAPI
Client-side SPA fetching JSON from an API
rebuild_decisions.constraints_from_source: Jinja2Templates used as FastAPI dependency in browse endpoint
